ordered_diagnoses: Plasma cell myeloma with liver involvement

facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman
IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma (Durie-Salmon IIA, R-ISS II)
previously treated with multiple chemotherapy regimens, two autologous stem-cell transplants, thalidomide maintenance, and focal bone radiotherapy
asymptomatic with stable vital signs
no hepatosplenomegaly on examination
Liver function tests, including ALT, AST, ALP, GGTP, and bilirubin, were within normal limits
a 35 mm lesion in the right hepatic lobe showed an SUVmax of 6.1
a 17 mm lesion in segment VI with moderately increased T2 signal, decreased T1 signal, weak heterogeneous contrast enhancement, and restricted diffusion
favoring a non-characteristic malignant lesion
lesion size decreased to 10 mm
lesion size enlarged to 57 × 46 mm
a percutaneous liver biopsy was planned to establish a definitive diagnosis

concepts.why: The patient has a history of liver lesions with increased SUVmax and heterogeneous contrast enhancement, favoring a malignant lesion.
The patient has a history of plasma cell myeloma and the liver lesion has shown significant growth, suggesting possible metastasis.
The patient has a liver lesion with restricted diffusion and heterogeneous contrast enhancement, which could be consistent with an abscess.
The patient has a liver lesion with increased T2 signal and decreased T1 signal, which could be consistent with FNH.
The patient has a liver lesion with increased T2 signal and decreased T1 signal, which could be consistent with a hemangioma.
The patient has a liver lesion with increased SUVmax and heterogeneous contrast enhancement, which could be consistent with ICC.
The patient has a liver lesion with restricted diffusion and heterogeneous contrast enhancement, which could be consistent with sarcoidosis.
